hook: My husband has **stopped supporting me.** What can I do?

slides.title: Yes, if he **neglects** you.
slides.body: If a husband with sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain a wife who can't maintain herself, a Magistrate can order a monthly allowance. A divorced wife who hasn't remarried counts too.

timeline.text: The Magistrate can order **interim maintenance** plus the expenses of the case.
The interim plea is decided, as far as possible, from service of notice.
Payable from the order date or, if ordered, from the **application date.**

slides.title: Where can you **file?**
list: Where he last lived with you
slides.ref: BNSS 2023 · Sec 145(1); Legal Services Authorities Act 1987 · Sec 12(c)

slides.title: He doesn't pay? **Jail possible.**
slides.body: The Magistrate can issue a warrant, and for each month's unpaid allowance, jail him for up to one month or until he pays. Apply within **one year** of the amount falling due.

slides.title: When a wife **can't** claim.
list: She refuses to live with him without sufficient reason
They live apart by mutual consent
slides.note: His second marriage: just ground to refuse

slides.title: Hindu wife? **More options.**
list: During a divorce case: interim maintenance and case expenses
At or after the decree: permanent alimony
A Hindu wife can claim maintenance for life
slides.ref: Hindu Marriage Act 1955 · Sec 24, 25; Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act 1956 · Sec 18(1)
slides.note: Uttarakhand: State's Uniform Civil Code applies

slides.title: Facing **domestic violence?**
slides.body: Under the DV Act, a Magistrate can order monetary relief, including maintenance for you and your children, as a lump sum or monthly payments. It must be adequate, fair and reasonable.
slides.ref: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 · Sec 20(1)(d), 20(2), 20(3)

sources: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 – Section 18 (JHALSA maintenance FAQ)
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 – Section 20
caption:
Husband not supporting you? The law gives a wife a right to maintenance. 👇

1️⃣ If a husband with sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain a wife who can't maintain herself, a Magistrate can order a monthly allowance (BNSS Sec 144)
2️⃣ A divorced wife who hasn't remarried can claim too
3️⃣ Interim maintenance and case expenses can be ordered while the case is pending
4️⃣ If he doesn't pay, he can be jailed for up to a month for each unpaid month; apply within one year
5️⃣ Hindu wives can also claim under the Hindu Marriage Act and Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act; DV Act victims can get monetary relief
6️⃣ Women are entitled to free legal aid from Legal Services Authorities
⚠️ In Uttarakhand, the State's Uniform Civil Code, 2024 now governs marriage and divorce of residents (except Scheduled Tribes)

Source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Sec 144, 145); Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (Sec 24, 25); Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (Sec 18); Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (Sec 20); Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (Sec 12)
